AI Advice, Occupational Norms, and Job Search

We audit three large language models with about 31,000 requests for advice, written as residents of ten countries. Within each request pair, we vary the gender of the requester and hold the remaining text fixed.

Preliminary results from a pilot study, October 2026. Please do not cite or circulate.

Two models recommend female-typed occupations more often to women

Share of clear answers recommending nursing or childcare work over work as an electrician or car mechanic. The right column reports the gap in percentage points with its 95 percent confidence interval, in bold where the interval excludes zero.

Advice attributed to a typical resident is far more traditional

The occupational question, posed as a request for the model's own recommendation and as a question about what “a randomly chosen person in [country]” would recommend. Asking what the requester should do changes the gap little (Section 1 below).

A survey statement reverses GPT-5.6 Luna's recommendations

After the sentence “X out of 100 people in [country] agree that some jobs are better suited to men and others to women,” GPT-5.6 Luna recommends nursing or childcare work to men in about half of cases or more and almost never to women. Under a placebo sentence on coffee consumption, the gap keeps its baseline sign. The gaps of the other two models rise with X (Section 2).

Advice varies little with country-level gender attitudes

Occupational advice gap by country against the share of World Values Survey respondents who agree that “when jobs are scarce, men should have more right to a job than women.” Only DeepSeek V4 Flash shows a slope whose 95 percent interval excludes zero. The models' own estimates of these shares correlate with the survey at 0.78 to 0.91 (Section 3).

1 All decisions and question forms

Select a decision, question form and model. Countries are ordered by the share of World Values Survey respondents who agree with the statement most closely related to the decision.

2 Survey information

Requests for Jordan, India, Italy and the United States with an added sentence that reports survey agreement with occupational gender roles, a placebo sentence on coffee consumption, or neither.

3 Beliefs about local attitudes

Model estimates of how many of 100 residents agree with four World Values Survey statements. The estimates preserve the ranking of countries but are compressed toward the middle of the scale.

4 Design and estimation

One request pair and the verbatim responses of GPT-5.6 Luna. In 127 of the 360 occupational pairs in which GPT-5.6 Luna gave a clear answer to both versions, it recommended the female-typed occupation to the woman and the male-typed occupation to the man. It never made the opposite recommendation.

Sample. GPT-5.6 Luna, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite and DeepSeek V4 Flash, queried in English through OpenRouter, with requests written as residents of Albania, India, Indonesia, Italy, Jordan, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, South Korea and the United States. Each request appears in three wordings and in both option orders.

Estimation. For each request, we compute the difference between the outcome for the female and the male version, average over repetitions and requests, and report 95 percent confidence intervals based on variation across requests. Responses that do not choose an option are excluded. Responses are coded with a rule-based parser, validated by hand against several hundred responses. The analysis is exploratory and was not pre-registered.
